<details>
The script `raspberrypi-bootloader-install` is a bash helper designed to install Raspberry Pi bootloader files for either the "legacy" or "rpi4" board lineup. It performs input validation on the first argument, ensuring it is either "legacy" or "rpi4", and exits with an error if not. It checks for the existence of the source directory under `/usr/lib/raspberrypi/` and ensures exactly one suitable FAT partition exists at common mount points (`/boot`, `/boot/efi`, `/efi`). 

The installation process uses a safe atomic-like update method: files are first copied with a `.new` extension, synced to storage, and then atomically renamed to overwrite the originals. This prevents corruption in case of interruption. A trap ensures cleanup of partial `.new` files on exit. All operations are confined to the target mount point and the known source path. There are no network operations, no use of dangerous code evaluation (like `eval`), no obfuscation, and no unauthorized file access.

The script follows safe system administration practices and is consistent with expected behavior for a bootloader installation utility in an AUR package. It does not exhibit any characteristics of a supply chain attack.
